definition: Arabic packs what English spreads across words into single tokens: وسيكتبونها ("and they will write it") is one orthographic word.
details: Arabic packs what English spreads across words into single tokens: وسيكتبونها ("and they will write it") is one orthographic word. Consequences everywhere: higher tokenizer fertility, sparser word statistics, harder exact-match retrieval, and error metrics that need character-level views.

explainer.lead: Arabic packs into single orthographic words what English spreads across several: وسيكتبونها means "and they will write it" as one token. This shapes tokenization, statistics, retrieval, and error measurement.

tiers.eli5: Some languages squeeze a whole phrase into one written word, so counting words stops matching counting meaning.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers face higher tokenizer fertility, sparser word statistics, harder exact-match retrieval, and error metrics that need character-level views. Treating Arabic like English at the word level is the common pitfall.
tiers.paperLevel: Characterised by many morphemes per orthographic token; consequences include higher tokenizer fertility and sparser word statistics, measured with character-level views.

explainer.example: The single Arabic word وسيكتبونها carries conjunction, future tense, verb, subject, and object in one token.
